what: Western Digital makes hard disk drives for data centres. After spinning off its flash memory business as Sandisk in 2025, it is now focused on high-capacity drives that store cloud and AI data cheaply.
customers: Cloud and hyperscale data centre operators, enterprise storage vendors and video surveillance firms.
money: high-capacity nearline hard drives for cloud storage
drives for PCs, external storage and surveillance
moat: One of only two remaining hard drive makers at scale, with factories, patents and head technology that cannot be rebuilt quickly.
risks: Hard drive demand has swung sharply between boom and bust in past cycles
Flash storage continues to take share in applications where speed matters
Demand is concentrated among a few cloud buyers
It is a smaller company after the Sandisk separation
opportunities: AI data centres need bulk storage at the lowest cost per terabyte, which favours hard drives
Only two suppliers has kept pricing firm through this cycle
Revenue grew about 36% in the last financial year with very high margins
watch: Exabytes shipped and pricing per terabyte, plus progress on next-generation recording technology.
